flashcards.subject: Databases
flashcards.front: Relational Normal Forms (1NF → BCNF) & Lossless Decompositions
flashcards.back:
For functional dependency X → Y in relation R:
• 1NF: Atomic attribute values.
• 2NF: 1NF + No partial dependency (non-prime depends on subset of candidate key).
• 3NF: 2NF + For every X → Y, X is Superkey OR Y is Prime attribute.
• BCNF: For every non-trivial X → Y, X MUST be a Superkey.
• Lossless Join Condition: (R1 ∩ R2) → R1 OR (R1 ∩ R2) → R2 (Common attribute is a superkey of R1 or R2).

flashcards.subject: Operating Systems
flashcards.front: Critical Section 3 Gold Invariants & Peterson's Solution
flashcards.back:
1. Mutual Exclusion (Mandatory): Only 1 process inside CS at a time.
2. Progress (Mandatory): Selection of who enters next is decided only by processes not in remainder.
3. Bounded Waiting (Fairness): Finite bound on entries allowed to others after request.
• Peterson's uses flag[i]=true and turn=j (courtesy variable) to satisfy all 3 for 2 processes.

flashcards.subject: Algorithms
flashcards.front: Comparison-Based Sorting Theoretical Bounds & Hashing Collisions
flashcards.back:
• Any comparison sort requires Ω(n log n) comparisons in the worst case (decision tree height log2(n!) ≈ n log2(n)).
• QuickSort: Best/Avg O(n log n), Worst O(n²) (already sorted with extremal pivot).
• Open Addressing with Linear Probing suffers from Primary Clustering.

flashcards.subject: Algorithms
flashcards.front: 0/1 Knapsack vs Fractional Knapsack Algorithmic Paradigms
flashcards.back:
• Fractional Knapsack: Solved via GREEDY strategy (sort by Value/Weight ratio). Time: O(n log n).
• 0/1 Knapsack: Items cannot be split. Solved via DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING. Time: O(n · W) (Pseudo-polynomial; NP-Complete in general).
• Longest Common Subsequence (LCS): DP time O(m · n), space O(min(m, n)).

flashcards.subject: Computer Networks
flashcards.front: CSMA/CD Minimum Frame Size & Sliding Window Efficiency
flashcards.back:
• CSMA/CD Minimum Frame Length: L ≥ 2 · T_prop · Bandwidth = 2 · (Distance / v) · B
• Stop-and-Wait Efficiency: η = 1 / (1 + 2a) where a = T_prop / T_trans
• Go-Back-N Efficiency: η = N / (1 + 2a) (Sender Window = N, Receiver Window = 1)
• Selective Repeat Efficiency: η = N / (1 + 2a) (Sender Window = N, Receiver Window = N; Max N = 2^(k-1) for k sequence bits).

flashcards.subject: Operating Systems
flashcards.back:
• 4 Coffman Conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait.
• Deadlock-Free Guarantee: For n processes each needing at most k resource instances from m total resources, system is deadlock-free if:
  m ≥ n · (k - 1) + 1
• Safe State ⟹ No Deadlock. Unsafe State ⇏ Deadlock (only potential deadlock).

flashcards.subject: Compiler Design
flashcards.front: Data Flow Analysis: Constant Propagation & Liveness Analysis
flashcards.back:
• Constant Propagation: Forward data-flow analysis finding variables with constant values at compile time.
• Liveness Analysis: Backward data-flow analysis checking if variable x is used before being redefined along some execution path (used in register allocation).
• Common Subexpression Elimination: Removes duplicate evaluations of identical expressions using DAGs.

flashcards.subject: Compiler Design
flashcards.back:
• S-Attributed Definition:
  - Uses ONLY Synthesized attributes (computed from children in parse tree).
  - Evaluated Bottom-Up during LR parsing.
• L-Attributed Definition:
  - Allows Synthesized AND restricted Inherited attributes.
  - An inherited attribute of node X_j can depend ONLY on: Parent attribute, or left siblings (X_1, ..., X_{j-1}).
  - Evaluated in a single Top-Down Depth-First left-to-right pass.

flashcards.subject: Computer Networks
flashcards.front: IPv4 Subnetting, CIDR & Fragmentation Offset Rules
flashcards.back:
• CIDR /n notation: Subnet Mask has n leading 1s. Usable host IPs = 2^(32 - n) - 2 (subtract Network ID and Broadcast ID).
• IPv4 Fragmentation Offset: Measured in 8-byte units! Offset = (Original Byte Position) / 8.
• More Fragments (MF) flag = 1 for all fragments except the last one (MF = 0).

flashcards.subject: Algorithms
flashcards.front: Dijkstra vs Bellman-Ford vs Floyd-Warshall Comparison
flashcards.back:
• Dijkstra: Single source, non-negative weights only. Min-Heap time: O((V + E) log V).
• Bellman-Ford: Single source, handles negative weights & detects negative cycles. Time: O(V · E).
• Floyd-Warshall: All-pairs shortest path, DP dynamic matrix. Time: Θ(V³).
• DAG Shortest Path: Topological Sort + Edge relaxation. Time: O(V + E) (handles negative weights!).
